problem_text:
A logistics firm is preparing a shipment to be dispatched via a cargo aircraft with a maximum payload capacity. They must select a combination of cargo containers to maximize total revenue while adhering to the aircraft's weight limit.

The available containers are:
* Container A: weight 2 tonnes, revenue 31 thousand dollars
* Container B: weight 7 tonnes, revenue 169 thousand dollars
* Container C: weight 6 tonnes, revenue 210 thousand dollars
* Container D: weight 46 tonnes, revenue 75 thousand dollars
* Container E: weight 50 tonnes, revenue 281 thousand dollars
* Container F: weight 13 tonnes, revenue 152 thousand dollars
* Container G: weight 19 tonnes, revenue 91 thousand dollars
* Container H: weight 12 tonnes, revenue 125 thousand dollars
* Container I: weight 9 tonnes, revenue 76 thousand dollars
* Container J: weight 15 tonnes, revenue 142 thousand dollars
* Container K: weight 32 tonnes, revenue 165 thousand dollars
* Container L: weight 10 tonnes, revenue 148 thousand dollars
* Container M: weight 14 tonnes, revenue 50 thousand dollars
* Container N: weight 9 tonnes, revenue 218 thousand dollars
* Container O: weight 12 tonnes, revenue 111 thousand dollars
* Container P: weight 38 tonnes, revenue 18 thousand dollars
* Container Q: weight 23 tonnes, revenue 285 thousand dollars
* Container R: weight 43 tonnes, revenue 255 thousand dollars

Furthermore, due to contractual obligations, exactly one of Container A and Container B must be included in the shipment.

If Container C is selected, the effective payload capacity of the aircraft is diminished by 10 tonnes.
The aircraft can carry at most 251 tonnes. The firm must determine which containers to load.
